description:
A Context Product example's DECLARED PRODUCT GATES, with CLOSED keys.

Ruled at Gate 1 of Phase 24.4 (`D-IMPL-225` amendment 3, Dave, 2026-08-31),
under `D-IMPL-224`: a product's gates are a DECLARED ARTIFACT plus CI
coverage. There is no `ProductGate` Protocol, no serve path for them, and the
SDK's universal gates stay the only serve-time gates. This schema describes
the declaration; it adds nothing to the fabric.

WHY THIS FILE IS NOT AN SDK ARTIFACT CLASS

CLAUDE.md section 11: the SDK never invents a schema for a namespace that is
not its own, and a product-level gate roster is the PRODUCT's namespace. So
this is not a member of `SDK_ARTIFACT_CLASSES`, it carries no
`x-ccf-class-id`, and it is not emitted by `tools/dump_schemas.py`. A gate
roster is a fact about one example's obligations, authored by that example
and reviewed with it.

WHY THIS FILE SITS IN A SUBDIRECTORY

`tools/dump_schemas.py` walks the TOP-LEVEL `docs/schemas/*.json` glob
(`:335`) against the SDK's artifact-class population and calls
`orphan.unlink()` (`:399`) on any committed file that population does not
emit; `tests/cli/test_schema_export.py:145` asserts exactly that behavior.
A hand-authored file at the top level would therefore be DELETED as an
orphan the next time anyone ran `make schemas` -- and deleted quietly,
because removing an orphan is the tool working rather than failing.

The glob is not recursive, so a subdirectory is outside it. That is the whole
reason for the path, and it is what stops the two locked criteria of this
phase contradicting each other: the roster is committed under `docs/schemas/`
as criterion 43 requires, and nothing under `src/` changes as criterion 49
requires.

WHAT IS NOT HERE, DELIBERATELY

NO COVERAGE CHECKER. Enforcement -- the assertion that each declared id has
an EXECUTING test rather than merely a matching string somewhere -- is Phase
24.5's, not this phase's. `D-IMPL-224` is explicit that the checker must
require an executing test and never an `id in file` substring match, because
measured across this ladder 40 product-level gate ids exist across four
products while a grep for those ids across `src/` and `runtime/` returns 0.
A schema cannot make that distinction; a checker can, and it is scheduled.

NO GATE COUNT FIELD. A roster is the truth and a cardinality is not: a right
count with a wrong member audits clean forever. `gates` is the roster, and a
consumer wanting a count derives it.

WHY `observed_red` IS REQUIRED BUT NULLABLE

A gate that has never been seen red is not evidence that it runs. Measured
across this ladder, fourteen declared gates once sat idle behind exactly that
assumption. Making the key REQUIRED and the value NULLABLE is what makes an
unsabotaged gate VISIBLY unsabotaged rather than absent: a reader scanning a
roster sees `observed_red: null` and knows the obligation is outstanding,
where an omitted key would look like a gate with nothing left to do.

class_id.description: The declaring product's own class id, in its own namespace.

gates.description: Every gate this product declares, as DATA. The specification's prose gate table is the machine source for nothing: CI must not depend on parsing prose out of Markdown, which is the fragility this artifact exists to escape.

criterion.description: The locked ROADMAP success-criterion number this gate discharges. One gate per criterion and one criterion per gate; the bijection is asserted by the declaring product's own test, not here, because a schema cannot see the roster as a whole.

id.description: The gate id. The pattern is the one measured across this ladder's four products -- two to four uppercase letters, a hyphen, `G`, and two digits.

observed_red.description: The record of the gate having been WATCHED TO FAIL, or `null` if it has not been. Required as a key so an unsabotaged gate is visibly unsabotaged rather than absent.

commit.description: The commit at which the observation was recorded.

date.description: The date the sabotage was applied and the failure watched.

result.description: What was observed when the sabotage was applied. A gate recorded as passing without this is a gate nobody has watched fail.

sabotage.description: What is MUTATED to make this gate fail. Named per gate rather than described generically, because a check that reads a token present in both the compliant and the violating case is measuring vocabulary rather than content -- and the only way to tell the two apart is to apply a specific mutation and watch.

statement.description: The assertion, in the words the approved specification gives it.

test.description: A `path.py::Symbol` reference to the test that executes this gate, in the citation form `D-IMPL-114` rules for this tree — never `path.py:LINE`, because a line anchor is wrong the moment code moves. The earlier pattern `^[^ ]+::[^ ]+$` checked only that a separator was present, so `tests/x.py:123::test_name` satisfied it: a line-anchored citation wearing a node id's shape. Found by the 2026-09-01 close panel. The declaring product's own test resolves the reference against a real `pytest --collect-only`; this pattern is what stops a malformed one reaching that check at all.

product.description: The product class these gates are declared for.

test_naming_convention.description: How a gate id maps onto the test function name that executes it, stated as data. Measured across this ladder, three products used three conventions and a coverage instrument keyed on function names reported 0 of 8, 0 of 9 and 0 of 9 falsely -- so the convention is DECLARED here rather than inferred by a checker.

semver.description: The roster's own version lane. A gate roster is a Control Plane artifact and changing what a product must prove changes what the product claims, so it versions like any other.

title: ProductGateRoster
